clue.text: Book by Houdini perhaps a best seller?

parts.note: the escapologist Harry Houdini was famous for breaking out of locks, a lock buster

explanation.surface: A question whether a volume written by the great escapologist sold in huge numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks Houdini as one example of a lock buster.
explanation.definitionFit: A blockbuster is a hugely successful book or film, a commercial smash.

clue.text: Change way locks can be arranged

definitions.meaning: old British slang for a shilling, so loose coins or money
a short haircut, a style for the locks of hair

explanation.surface: Advice on altering how the locks on a door are set up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'locks' looks like door hardware, but it means hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Bob is slang for a shilling coin, and also a short hairstyle cut level round the head.

clue.text: Gold coin found in path

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
a bit is a small coin, as in a threepenny bit

explanation.surface: A gold coin turns up lying on a footpath.
explanation.definitionFit: An orbit is the curved course or path of a body circling another.

clue.text: In habit of bagpiper, perhaps, to preserve old blowing power

indicators.note: to preserve something is to keep it safe inside, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a kilt is the usual dress of a Scottish piper; habit means clothing here
on can mean in, as in on the team

explanation.surface: Something in a piper's outfit keeps the old wind power of the bagpipes going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blowing power' suggests bagpipes, but it means explosive force; ON from 'In' goes at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiloton is a unit of explosive force equal to a thousand tons of TNT, a measure of blast.

clue.text: Luke doing works not divine

indicators.note: works as a verb means operates on, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Saint Luke's activities are said to be less than holy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works' looks like the noun for deeds; it is the anagram signal on LUKE DOING.
explanation.definitionFit: Ungodlike means lacking the qualities of a god, so not divine.

clue.text: Measured performance sees firm finally break even

indicators.note: one piece breaking another splits it open and sits in the gap

parts.note: even means level, drawn, tied

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word firm

explanation.surface: A company's results show the firm just about breaking even.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break even' reads as a business phrase; 'break' puts M inside TIED. 'performance sees' joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Timed means measured by the clock, as in a timed run.

clue.text: Stripper finally shed clothes posh then diamonds brightly coloured

indicators.note: clothes as a verb means dresses or covers, so the first pieces wrap round another
finally picks the closing letter of the word Stripper

parts.note: a byre is a cowshed
U means upper-class, posh
D is the card abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A stripper finally takes off a posh outfit and then the jewellery, in vivid colours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' is the verb: R and BYRE together wrap round U, then D follows after 'then'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruby red is a deep vivid red, a bright colour named after the gem.

clue.text: Dress is short: I disapprove

indicators.note: short says the word lacks its final letter

parts.note: a tutu is a ballet dress

explanation.surface: Someone frowning at a too-brief hemline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' looks like a description of the dress's length; it cuts the last letter from TUTU.
explanation.definitionFit: Tut is an exclamation of mild disapproval or impatience.

clue.text: Cheers when ramblers go in line, crossing over bridge

indicators.note: the ramblers going in means they enter the other piece

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks, cheers
ravers are people who rave, talk wildly and ramble

explanation.surface: Applause as a walking group files across a bridge in single line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ramblers' suggests walkers, but means those who rave on; 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A traversal is a passage across something, such as a bridge or a mountain face.

clue.text: Operetta that several must hear

definitions.meaning: a comic opera by Gilbert and Sullivan, a light Victorian stage work
a case heard by twelve citizens sitting together in court

explanation.surface: A light opera that a group of people are obliged to listen to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hear' is the legal sense: a jury hears a case.
explanation.definitionFit: Gilbert and Sullivan's one-act comic opera, and also the court process where a panel of citizens hears evidence.

clue.text: Sweet one pops in one's mouth

definitions.text: Sweet one pops in one's mouth

parts.words: Sweet one pops in one's mouth
parts.note: reads as popping a sweet into the mouth, but this chewy confection is blown into bubbles that pop

explanation.surface: Tossing a candy into the mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pops in' looks like 'puts in'; it is the bubble bursting.
explanation.definitionFit: Chewing gum that can be blown into bubbles which burst in the mouth.

clue.text: Blend honey and jam if starting to make cake

indicators.note: starting picks the opening letter of each of the five words before it

explanation.surface: A recipe step: mix honey and jam to begin a bake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make' links wordplay to definition; a bhaji is an Indian fritter, fairly called a cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A bhaji is a small fried Indian patty of spiced vegetables in batter, a savoury cake.

clue.text: Made different, damaging allegations about arts centre

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: mud is scandalous accusation, as in mud-slinging
the Tate is the London art gallery

explanation.surface: Damaging claims about a cultural venue changed things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arts centre' looks like a middle-letter pick, but is the Tate gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: Mutated means altered in form or nature, changed.

clue.text: Some PC parent on the committee

parts.note: a mother is a parent
a board is a governing committee

explanation.surface: A politically correct parent serves on a committee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'PC' suggests politically correct, but means a personal computer; 'on' places one piece before the other.
explanation.definitionFit: The main circuit board inside a computer, part of every personal computer.

clue.text: Traveller rudely rebuffed entertaining writer

indicators.note: rebuffed says the hidden letters are read backwards
entertaining means holding as a guest, so the words keep the answer within them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A traveller rudely rejects an amusing author.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'entertaining writer' as the definition, leaving the hidden word no indicator; 'entertaining' holds the run LLERRUD inside 'Traveller rudely', and 'rebuffed' turns it.
explanation.definitionFit: Gerald Durrell wrote comic memoirs of animal collecting and his brother Lawrence novels; both are authors.

clue.text: Hearing match lost makes one cross

indicators.note: on hearing means the words are judged by how they are spoken

parts.note: a tie is a match, gone means lost

explanation.surface: A tribunal hearing goes against someone, leaving them angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearing' looks like a court hearing; 'cross' looks like angry but means a hybrid.
explanation.definitionFit: A tigon is the hybrid offspring of a male tiger and a lioness, a crossbred animal.

clue.text: Design trap: that's game keeper's area

parts.note: a design is an aim, a goal
trap is slang for mouth

explanation.surface: A plan for a snare is how a gamekeeper looks after the estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game keeper' reads as gamekeeper; split, it is the goalkeeper in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: The goalmouth is the area right in front of a goal, the goalkeeper's patch.

clue.text: Tommy dies after ordering blowing of trumpet

indicators.note: after being put in order, the letters take a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A soldier dies after orders to sound the bugle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tommy' looks like the British soldier; it is fodder with DIES. 'blowing of trumpet' is boasting, blowing one's own trumpet.
explanation.definitionFit: Immodesty is boastfulness, the habit of blowing one's own trumpet.

clue.text: His orderly table to finish in confusion, see

indicators.note: one piece sits in the other

parts.note: a melee is a confused brawl
to end is to finish
V is the abbreviation for vide, Latin for see

explanation.surface: A man's tidy table ends up in a mess, look.
explanation.walkthrough: Mendeleev devised the periodic table, ordering the elements.
explanation.definitionFit: Dmitri Mendeleev created the periodic table of elements, an orderly table he is named by.

clue.text: Wounded, one cuts dash in battle

indicators.note: one piece cutting another goes into it

parts.note: elan is dash, flair
lame means injured, wounded
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A wounded soldier slices through with flair during combat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dash' looks like a sprint, but is spirit or élan.
explanation.definitionFit: El Alamein was a decisive Second World War battle in Egypt.

clue.text: Embarrassed Brit, say, getting seven days inside

indicators.note: inside places one piece within the other

parts.note: a Brit is a British music industry award
WK is the abbreviation for week

explanation.surface: A British person, red-faced, gets a week in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brit' looks like a Briton but is a Brit Award.
explanation.definitionFit: Awkward means uncomfortable or embarrassed in a social situation.

clue.text: Sauce running left valuable metal dish

indicators.note: in an across clue running leftward means read from right to left

parts.note: lip is cheek, sauce, impudence
AU is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Sauce runs off a dish made of precious metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sauce' looks like a liquid; it is cheek.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilau is a rice dish cooked in stock with spices.

clue.text: Protection from light slap, or a thrashing

indicators.note: thrashing means beating about, so the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Choosing between a light slap and a beating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light' looks like the adjective with slap; it belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasol is a sunshade, protection from sunlight.

clue.text: Peasant to practise opposite of nepotism?

definitions.meaning: to knock relatives out instead of favouring them

explanation.surface: A country labourer accused of favouritism in reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: Nepotism favours relatives; to bump kin is to oust them.
explanation.definitionFit: A bumpkin is an awkward country person, a yokel or peasant.

clue.text: Irish girl's husband leading rising

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: main means chief, leading

explanation.surface: An Irish woman's husband is getting up first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading' looks like a position word; it is MAIN. 'girl's' gives the definition and 'is' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Niamh is an Irish girl's name, from a heroine of Irish legend.

clue.text: Newcomer to wheel in crude material

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other

parts.note: earthy means coarse, crude
L is the learner driver, new to the steering wheel

explanation.surface: A novice potter at the wheel up to the elbows in raw clay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crude material' reads as one phrase; split, 'material' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthly means material, of this world rather than the spiritual.

clue.text: Row when two pieces of headgear short

indicators.note: short says each piece loses its last letter

parts.note: a hood and a hat are two items worn on the head

explanation.surface: An argument breaks out over two hats being too small.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts D from HOOD and T from HAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoo-ha is a commotion or fuss, a row.

clue.text: African city forbidden no end of meat? Hamburger's OK

indicators.note: no means without, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: tabu is a spelling of taboo, forbidden

indicators.note: end of picks the closing letter of the word meat

parts.note: ja is German for yes, said by someone from Hamburg

explanation.surface: An African city bans meat, but a German is fine with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamburger' is a person from Hamburg, not a burger.
explanation.definitionFit: Abuja is the capital city of Nigeria.

clue.text: The philosopher's stone gets sudden prominence abroad

parts.note: A.J. Ayer was a British philosopher
a rock is a stone

explanation.surface: The legendary philosopher's stone suddenly becomes famous overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: The philosopher's stone is the alchemists' goal; here it is Ayer's rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Ayers Rock (Uluru) is a huge sandstone monolith rising abruptly from the Australian plain.

clue.text: Schoolboy joke?

explanation.surface: A schoolboy prank.
explanation.definitionFit: Kid means a child, and as a verb to tease or fool someone.

clue.text: How foolish of me to make you scuttle back

indicators.note: back says the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a hod is a coal scuttle

explanation.surface: Someone apologises for making you hurry away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scuttle' looks like the verb to scurry; it is a coal container.
explanation.definitionFit: Doh is an exclamation admitting one's own stupidity.

clue.text: Aviator survived carrying a type of bomb back to ground

indicators.note: back says the combined piece is read in reverse
carrying means holding inside

parts.note: lived means survived
H as in H-bomb, the hydrogen bomb
to land is to come to ground

explanation.surface: A pilot survived despite carrying a bomb back to base.
explanation.walkthrough: LIVED carrying A H is LIVAHED; 'back' turns that to DEHAVIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Geoffrey de Havilland was a pioneering British aviator and aircraft designer.
